items.name: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
items.title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
items.description: Speech brain-computer interfaces (speech BCIs) translate neural activity into language, offering a path towards restoring speech for people with paralysis and, more broadly, enabling new forms of natural human-computer interaction. Despite this promise, the field lacks a common measure of progress because systems use different datasets, recording methods, types of speech, and vocabularies, so their reported scores are rarely comparable. items.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
items.description: Recent web agents use world models for test-time action selection by sampling candidate actions, predicting the resulting web states, and ranking them with a ranker model or a Process Reward Model (PRM). items.title: Graph Machine: Towards Better Pretraining via Edges
items.description: We introduce the Graph Machine (GM), an architecture that maintains an $O(n)$-sized state and accesses it through sparse, dynamic routing. Unlike methods with fixed-size states or sparse but static routing, GM preserves $O(n)$ complexity in its sparse layers without restricting the potentially accessible state size to $O(1)$. items.title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
items.description: Ordinary differential equations (ODEs) underlie models in science and engineering, and many applications need derivatives of their solutions with respect to parameters. Ensembles of independent trajectories suit graphics processing units (GPUs), but current GPU software forces a trade-off: the fastest ensemble solvers cannot be differentiated in reverse mode at the speed they solve, and the solvers built for differentiation solve more slowly. items.title: Towards Trustworthy Autonomous Robots: An Explainable AI-Based Decision Framework
items.description: Autonomous robots powered by deep learning face a fundamental auditability challenge: when incidents occur, investigators cannot reconstruct why the system made specific decisions. items.name: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
items.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
items.description: Harnessing naturally occurring feedback from user interactions offers a promising learning signal for Large Language Models (LLMs). However, recent studies suggest this feedback is inherently noisy and difficult to leverage effectively. items.title: Improved Gradient Descent Lower Bounds Beyond Nesterov

items.name: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security
items.title: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security
items.description: LLMs are trained to generate natural language. However, various strands of evidence indicate that an LLM's externalized linguistic outputs and mechanistically-extracted linguistic features can be an unreliable lens for understanding internal model computation. items.name: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
items.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
items.description: Competitive programming has become a key test of large language model reasoning, with international competitions such as IOI and ICPC representing its most challenging settings. items.title: AI Contextual Measurement for Recovering Individual and Group-Level Effects: Validation Against Survey Measures and an Occupational Application
items.description: Researchers increasingly use artificial intelligence to construct measures of social, organizational, and occupational characteristics that are absent from conventional surveys. items.name: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
items.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
items.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for large language model (LLM) post-training, but its reliance on coarse outcome rewards leads to limited guidance on intermediate reasoning processes. items.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
items.description: Root cause analysis (RCA) is a critical task in telecom network operations, but diagnosing performance degradations in modern 5G and emerging 6G networks remains challenging due to complex cross-layer dependencies. items.title: frb100-40 After Two Decades: An Optimality Certificate and a Preregistered Search Study
items.description: For more than 20 years, the Model-RB benchmark frb100-40 remained an open challenge; since 2014, its public record had stood at 99 of 100 variables. We give a directly checkable 100-vertex independent set for its 4,000-vertex graph. items.name: Dutch Books for Language Models
items.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
items.description: People increasingly use language models to support life decisions. Many such decisions involve a probabilistic forecast: How likely is a major life event, a natural disaster, or an economic outcome? items.title: DiscoSign: Discourse-Aware Text to Sign Language Gloss Translation
items.description: Sign language processing systems have traditionally operated at the sentence level, ignoring critical discourse phenomena fundamental to sign language comprehension. items.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
items.description: The performance of LLM-based agents is jointly shaped by the base model and the harness used when interacting with the environment. This exposes them to safety risks in both harmful final responses and multi-step execution trajectories. items.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
items.description: Evaluating LLM agents is essential for guiding their development, yet it has grown prohibitively expensive: a single pass of a frontier model over an agentic benchmark can cost hundreds to thousands of dollars, a price paid repeatedly across iterative development cycles. items.title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
items.description: Streaming video understanding is a critical capability for real-world applications, including embodied intelligence, autonomous driving, industrial monitoring, surveillance and early warning, and wearable assistants. items.title: HyperStyler: Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer via Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks
items.description: Low-resource authorship style transfer (LAST) aims to rewrite text into the style of an arbitrary target author using only a few reference examples while preserving the original meaning. items.title: From Reweighting to Rewriting: Unlocking the Intervention Effects of Influential Samples in Training Data Attribution
items.description: Training data attribution (TDA) aims to identify training examples that shape model behavior, but its intervention value depends on both which examples are selected and how they are modified. items.name: Do Tabular Foundation Models Know Physics? Contamination, Units, and the Deterministic Limit
items.title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Know Physics? Contamination, Units, and the Deterministic Limit
items.description: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) learn to fill in tables the way language models fill in text, and tables are arguably the format in which most physical measurement arrives. items.title: Measurement-Driven Sub-Network Selection for On-Premise Retrieval-Augmented Factory Agents
items.description: On-premise assistants can give factory workers conversational access to machine documentation, but models capable of the task rarely fit shop-floor hardware. items.title: Untangling the Mechanisms of Misleading Context in Medical Question Answering
items.description: Large language models now answer medical questions with expert-level performance. However, the context these systems act on can be misleading, and misleading context can corrupt a model's medical judgment. items.description: Multi-agent LLM systems commonly use an orchestrator to decompose a task for a team of workers and then improve through textual reflection. items.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
